comparator.name: Medical Informatics
comparator.sourceNotes: The Dutch-taught bachelor has 60 EC each year. The third year combines 18 EC of open electives, 18 EC of taught courses and a 24 EC internship and thesis. The regulations specify progression and a competency portfolio that must pass before the internship and thesis.
components: Entry to year two requires 48 EC from year one under the binding study advice rules.
Exchange of Health Data and Knowledge
The academic and professional competency portfolio is assessed during this course.
Entry to year three requires all 60 EC of year one and at least 48 EC from year two.
Choose one or more electives for 18 EC. Choices outside the preapproved list require Examination Board approval.
Pass the academic and professional competency portfolio before starting the internship and thesis. The regulations place both in the second semester of year three.

core: Health information systems, clinical information modelling and interoperable patient-data management
Programming, software engineering and user-centred applications for healthcare
Medical foundations, clinical reasoning, healthcare work and patient safety
Statistics, epidemiology, health-data analysis, AI and scientific research
adjacent: Digital health, remote monitoring and responsible healthcare innovation
Healthcare organisations, processes, entrepreneurship and strategic information management
questions: How can health data and information systems support safe clinical decisions and coordinated care?
How should useful, usable and responsible software be designed for patients and healthcare professionals?
How can statistics, AI and process analysis improve healthcare while respecting clinical and organisational realities?

alternatives.label: Health information systems & software
alternatives.labelReason: Programming, databases and software construction are the technical core. Epidemiology, research, ethics and digital strategy provide health and organisational context.
alternatives.concept: Study how software and data can support healthcare. Combine programming, databases and software design with epidemiology and research methods, and consider how organisations adopt new technology.
progression: Programming precedes Software Development and Algorithms & Data Structures. Data Science precedes Machine Learning and neural networks. Brain & Behavior prepares for evidence synthesis.

alternatives.label: Biomedical data, signals & machine learning
alternatives.labelReason: Anatomy, physiology and disease provide biomedical context for mathematics, signals, image processing and machine learning.
alternatives.concept: Use mathematics, computing and biomedical science to study health data, images and signals. Develop analytical methods alongside an understanding of the body and disease.
alternatives.distinctness: This option builds depth in biomedical science and mathematical analysis. The information-systems option emphasises software, data management and organisational change.
progression: Biomedical foundations precede anatomy, physiology and disease. Linear algebra and signal analysis prepare for image processing, while Mathematical Methods and Machine Learning precede neural networks.

alternatives.label: Health behaviour & digital innovation
alternatives.labelReason: Health psychology, epidemiology, communication and research provide the foundation for studying digital change and how people respond to it.
alternatives.concept: Study how people respond to health information and changes in care. Combine health psychology, behavioural research and persuasive communication with data analysis and digital strategy.
alternatives.distinctness: Health behaviour, mental health, communication and organisational change distinguish this option from software construction and biomedical modelling.
progression: Psychology and sociology provide foundations for health behaviour and social inquiry. Research Methods & Statistics and Brain & Behavior prepare for advanced evidence synthesis. Data science precedes Machine Learning.

Digital health, behaviour and healthcare innovation

blocks: Both use statistical models and study design. UCR focuses on health and behaviour experiments, while UvA pairs biostatistics with clinical epidemiology.
Both study population health, disease patterns and determinants. UvA connects these topics to its healthcare curriculum.
Both use programming to build working software. UvA applies it to healthcare applications.
Both study organising and retrieving data. UvA addresses how healthcare systems exchange information and knowledge.
Both use logic and formal reasoning. UvA applies these ideas to medical diagnosis.
Both study machine learning. UvA applies AI in the context of healthcare and clinical information.
Both analyse digital images. UCR uses general image-processing and computer-vision methods, while UvA covers medical imaging and signals.
Both develop software design and construction skills. UvA embeds software engineering in medical informatics.
Both develop ideas from user needs and consider how to implement them. UvA focuses on innovation in healthcare.
Both study organisational decisions about technology and change. UvA focuses on information management in healthcare.

selection.assessment: Three options cover health information systems and software, biomedical data and signals, and health behaviour and digital innovation. Software development is part of the closest option. The digital innovation option focuses on users, evidence and organisational change.

notes.text: UvA teaches healthcare software, exchange of clinical information and clinical reasoning in a dedicated degree. Its 24 EC internship and thesis connect those topics to practice. UCR offers related coursework in computing, data, biomedical science and behaviour.

audience.programmeDescription: Medical Informatics at the University of Amsterdam studies how software, data and information systems are used in healthcare. Students work with medical case studies and complete an internship and thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers related study in health information systems, biomedical data, and health behaviour and digital innovation. UvA combines these subjects in a dedicated healthcare degree with clinical casework and a required internship.
